kevin: heads-up — p99 decode latency jumped ~40ms on canary after yesterday's kernel-select change. stack looks host-heavy (writev + parse). @maya any idea? :eyes:

maya: saw that too but only on grpc paths. quick flame looked like a lot of small iovecs + tokenizer churn. attaching perf snippet in a sec.

kevin: ```
# perf top sample (stack bottom -> top)
grpc_writev -> http2_frame_write -> transport_layer::send_vec -> host_parse::tokenize -> request_parser::parse_prefix -> kvcache::evict_if_needed -> kernel_select::choose_kernels
# wall: host CPU dominates, syscall count up 2.4x
```

sophia: FYI batching heuristic change merged yesterday lowered auto-batch threshold to favor micro-batches for latency. that will increase number of write calls and smaller iovecs. could be the root.

alex: also noticed kvcache eviction rate spike aligns with p95 requests that have large prompt prefixes — cold kvcache causes extra parse + tokenization per request which amplifies syscall overhead. metric is `ingress.kvcache.evictions.per_minute` and `ingress.writev.iovec_len.p50/p95`.

kevin: ran quick metrics: `writev.iovec_len.p50` down ~30% on canary, ``writev.syscalls_per_req`` up ~2x. tokenization thread count per req increased too.

ryan: can we gate the kernel-select change + batching tweak separately? easiest test: revert batching heuristic first, keep kernel-select. if latency drops then batching is primary. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy (2026-03-19T22:13Z) -> kernel_select:v2, batch-heuristic:opt1 (rollout: 25% nodes)

maya: I'll roll a canary with kernel_select:v1 + batch-heuristic:opt1 to isolate. giving it 15m then posting results.

alex: aside from reverting, we should try coalescing small iovecs in the ingress proxy (merge adjacent small buffers before syscall). we had a prior patch for http1 that did this — low-risk and avoids syscall explosion for grpc writev. pseudo: ```
for buf in outbound_queue:
  if last_iovec_len + buf.len < COALESCE_LIMIT:
    append to last_iovec
  else:
    push new iovec
```

kevin: good idea. coalescing + throttle tokenization workers would reduce host CPU spikes while we root-cause kvcache behavior. also we should add per-shard kvcache eviction metrics to correlate.

sophia: tl;dr next actions: 1) isolate by reverting batching heuristic on canary (maya) 2) test writev coalesce in ingress proxy on separate canary (alex) 3) add kvcache-evict-per-shard metric + dashboard (sophia, owning).

kevin: added perf run command and trace link: http://perf.redwood.internal/1768001234/flame — will update when new canary numbers land. thanks all. :shipit:
